A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same M-STAR study. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and rendered figures support comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original self-evolving training experiments, benchmark evaluations, PRM analyses and training-dynamics measurements across three multimodal models.

after.justification: v2 retains the original training experiments, benchmark results and diagnostic analyses, including detailed results in its appendices.

M1.justification: The warm-up procedure, continuous optimizer and scheduler inheritance, answer filtering, PRM top-2 reranking and adaptive temperature selection remain unchanged. Moving the warm-up description to Appendix B does not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use MathV360K for training and in-domain evaluation, and evaluate on MathVista, M3CoT, MMStar-R, MMBench-R and AI2D. Newly mentioned tasks in related work are not evaluated by this study.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including SFT, iterative RFT, ReSTEM, random selection and PRM selection variants. RAFT and ReST-MCTS* are newly discussed as related work, not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 reduces the tracked diagnostics from four to three by removing Pass@K-minus-greedy accuracy. Dataset splits, training budgets, model configurations, rollout counts and temperature-selection settings otherwise remain unchanged; no experimental rerun is established.

E4.justification: v2 removes the exploration-gap analysis in v1 Figure 4b and its accompanying discussion. Other ablations and sensitivity analyses remain. The reasoning-step histogram moves from v1 Figure 2b to v2 Appendix F/Figure 6, so it is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-training-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance testing. Response-sampling counts remain unchanged and are not independent experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: Figure 3 materially changes a central dynamics result: v1 plots Pass@K declining from approximately 66% to 60%, whereas v2 plots it rising from approximately 45% to 63%. No corresponding setting change is explained, and the caption and discussion still describe decline. Benchmark table values otherwise match, including v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 6; the gap curves from v1 Figure 4b are removed.

T1.justification: The RL objectives in Equations 1–2, reward definitions in Equations 3–4 and Appendix D's step-label formula are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised; the removed gap diagnostic concerns empirical monitoring.

C1.justification: The revised abstract and introduction more explicitly claim to uncover the roots of performance saturation and attribute it to diminishing exploration, strengthening the earlier observational framing. The proposed framework, principal components and claimed model and benchmark coverage remain the same.

C2.justification: Appendix I adds an argument connecting M-STAR's filtering and reranking to rule-based RL and reward-hacking concerns. Appendix H also replaces the earlier qualified description of generally consistent subtask improvements with an all-subtasks assertion, despite retained regressions—for example, InternVL2's warm-up/M-STAR FQA scores remain 52.4/49.4.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly specifies that reasoning steps are counted by splitting on double newlines. Conversely, Section 3.3 omits v1's explicit 0.1 increment for the reward-threshold search, while retaining the selected threshold of 0.2. Most implementation details remain unchanged or are relocated.

R1.justification: Related work adds RAFT, ReST-MCTS*, DeepSeek-R1, SimpleRL-Zoo, B-STaR and Web-Shepherd, including a new discussion of compatibility with recent rule-based RL. References to DeepSeek-Prover-v1.5 and Qwen2.5-Math disappear with the shortened introduction. The broader positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, several introductory and explanatory paragraphs are tightened, warm-up material is consolidated in Appendix B, and appendix sections are reorganized. An Impact Statement is added. Most methodological prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column presentation to a two-column conference layout. v2 introduces a compact summary Table 4 while relocating the full original table to Appendix H, splits Figure 2 across main text and appendix, removes a Figure 4 panel, and redraws Figure 3 with different axes and trajectory.

improvement.justification: The compact presentation and updated related-work discussion offer modest benefits, but v2 introduces a Figure 3 trajectory that contradicts its caption and saturation argument. Appendix H's unqualified all-subtasks improvement statement also conflicts with retained results. These changes reduce evidential clarity and accuracy, while the unchanged method and benchmark evidence limit the overall deterioration.
